A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

it is possible to measure both the longitudinal and the transverse relaxation rates of nuclei at natural isotopic abundance using only three experiments and without the need to record a series of experiments at different mixing times.
we have developed an efficient method to determine the heteronuclear relaxation rates of natural abundance proteins.
the relaxation parameters of a peptide can be obtained in less than 1 hour, with a good signal‐to‐noise ratio and with a precision comparable to that obtained by classical methods.

the relaxation of nuclei can be measured in a fast and accurate way.
the relaxation parameters of a single spin can be determined in less than 1 h using a single‐channel spectrometer.
